title: Artis Paul, the high-note trumpet player
summary: Artis Paul, from Texas and a friend of Hot Lips Page, impressed Stan Kenton but drank and moved between Fields and Nat Towles.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Have we taken in all those sax men?
Yes. Can you think of anyone else?

I was trying to think. We mentioned Candy Johnson. While we're talking about fine sax men who have been through the band, I mentioned something about Artis Paul. Now Artis Paul was a very fine trumpet man, a tone man, out of Texas and he-- I believe it was Tyler or Corsicana--but anyway, he was closely in that vicinity of Hot Lips Page, that they had worked together. Sometimes you wouldn't get the best of Artis, but I think he got onto whiskey-- he's gone on now like all the rest of us have to do someday--but he was just awful bad on the whiskey.
Yeah, a moody guy, but a fine, fine note man. I think I showed you

a picture of Stan Kenton with myself, and we were listening to a playback--well, that was when Stan was attracted. He said who is making those high notes. Well, Artis Paul was on that session there and Stan Kenton was so impressed-- some of them could make the high notes and may be out of tune.
At different intervals, Artis was one of these come and go, he would be--another fine southwestern band which I know you know well, maybe as much or more than me, was Nat Towles.

I was with Nat Towles' band with Artis, a large percentage of 1944. Unfortunately he didn't get the recognition or the acclaim that he deserved. In another day Stan Kenton would have taken him with his band because he was as good a high note man as there was in the country, Artis Paul was.
Artis would switch from Nat and back to me, because he would always demand that salary.
He always wanted a little more money, and got it.
Yeah. And frankly, when he was sober he was worth it.
I'm going to show you some pictures of Artis, excellent pictures of Artis (inaudible).
